newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ex-Soviet dissident Sharansky to visit Russia.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet dissident Sharansky to visit Russia.

text.p: Former Soviet Jewish dissident Natan Sharansky goes to Russia this month as Israeli trade minister, returning for the first time since he was freed in a 1986 East-West prisoner swap, an official said on Thursday.
He postponed a scheduled visit last November after the sudden death of his wife's brother.
Sharansky, 48, arrives in Moscow on January 26 along with about 50 businessmen for a five-day visit aimed at boosting commercial ties between the two countries, ministry spokeswoman Haya Peri said.
He would meet Russian officials and old friends. But an Israeli spokesman said it was unclear whether Sharansky would visit his old prison.
"Israeli export today stands at $300 million and we see great potential for Israel in the Russian market," Peri told Reuters.
She said Israel hoped to begin exporting medical and agricultural equipment to Russia and could boost exports to $1 billion a year.
Sharansky was appointed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government in June after being elected to parliament at the head of a party of Russian immigrants.
He spent nine years in Soviet prisons before being allowed to leave for Israel in an East-West prisoner swap in 1986.
He was a founder member of the unofficial human rights Helsinki Group and first applied for an exit visa to Israel in 1973 but was refused for "security reasons".
After his imprisonment in 1978 for alleged espionage his wife Avital waged an international campaign for his release that made him one of the Soviet Union's most celebrated dissidents in the West.
He was released from jail on February 11, 1986, arriving in Israel to a hero's welcome that same night.
